clue.text: Funny: big fire prepared to do this to a guy?

definitions.text: to do this to a guy?

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready or worked up, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A comic aside: a big bonfire has been built, ready for a guy on the fifth of November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges FUNNY, BIG and FIRE together. A guy is the stuffed effigy of Guy Fawkes burnt on British bonfires every 5 November.
explanation.definitionFit: Burning a stuffed figure is exactly what a Bonfire Night crowd does to the guy on top of the pyre.

clue.text: Admit I hurt, joke backfiring

parts.note: 'ow!' is what someone says when they are hurt

indicators.note: a thing that backfires goes the opposite way, so the word for joke runs backwards

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that a joke went wrong and hurt them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfiring' sends the joke word the wrong way round; 'I hurt' is read as the cry a hurt person gives.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess something is a synonym phrase meaning to admit it.

clue.text: Tend curiously to hold fish like spaghetti?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round and hold the next piece inside them
done curiously, the letters come out in an odd, unexpected order

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Tending a pot of spaghetti in an odd way while fish is also in the mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' rearranges the four letters of 'Tend', and 'to hold' wraps them round the fishing verb. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Strands of spaghetti twist round one another, so a knotted, twisted mess is described this way.

clue.text: The only outlet for this game?

definitions.text: The only outlet for this game?

parts.words: The only outlet for this game?
parts.note: a business that is the only outlet for a product has exclusive control of the market, which is also the name of a property-trading board game

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether one shop alone sells a particular game.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclusive control by a single seller is the economic term that also names the famous property board game.

clue.text: Trim artwork to get shorter

indicators.note: trimming cuts a bit off the end, here the final letter of the word for artwork

parts.note: a drawing is a piece of artwork

explanation.surface: An instruction to crop a picture so that it is smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' takes the last letter G off DRAWING.
explanation.definitionFit: Days are said to draw in when they become shorter in autumn, an idiom for lessening daylight.

clue.text: Go over and about with the last thing in transport?

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
the hearse is the final vehicle anyone rides in, carrying the coffin to the funeral

explanation.surface: Rather a grim question about the final vehicle anyone travels in.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise or run through something again is a synonym for going over it.

clue.text: Worked, needing small addition to treasure

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a trove is a store of treasure, as in treasure trove

explanation.surface: Someone toiled to add a little to a hoard of treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing ... addition to' just sets S before TROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to work hard, so its past tense fits the past-tense verb.

clue.text: Where I may have problem, as athlete? Nonsense

definitions.text: Where I may have problem, as athlete?
definitions.meaning: athlete's foot is a fungal infection, so an athlete might have trouble in their own foot

explanation.surface: An athlete complains about a sore body part, then dismisses the whole idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a two-word exclamation of scorn is an idiom for dismissing something as nonsense.

clue.text: Film conflict in flight: one can't be seen

indicators.note: something that can't be seen has vanished, so that letter drops out of the word

parts.note: a flight of stairs; a stair is one step of it
I is the Roman numeral for one
wars are conflicts

explanation.surface: An aerial battle in which one combatant is invisible, as in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conflict in flight' suggests STAIR WARS; 'can't be seen' makes the I (one) vanish. The space-defence programme was also nicknamed this, a conflict in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous space-opera movie series by George Lucas is named this, so it is a film.

clue.text: The vintage of mother's ruin

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
the vintage of a wine is its age

explanation.surface: A remark about how old a bottle of gin, mother's ruin, is.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother's ruin is British slang for gin, which is why the surface reads like a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to harm it, a synonym of causing harm to it.

clue.text: Using TV and papers, say, is no extreme course

parts.note: via means by way of or using
television and newspapers are examples of the media

explanation.surface: Communicating through broadcast and print counts as a moderate approach.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means a middle road, a moderate path avoiding both extremes.

clue.text: To act like a woman, they say, I must talk freely

definitions.text: To act like a woman, they say

indicators.note: letters treated freely are let loose and rearranged without constraint

explanation.surface: A woman insists she must speak without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges I MUST TALK. The definition plays on the claim that women are good at doing several jobs at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Juggling several jobs at once is popularly said to be a female talent, hence acting like a woman.

clue.text: Time to tuck into what may be in bowl or basin

indicators.note: tucking into something places it inside, so the letter goes within the word

parts.note: soup is served in a bowl

explanation.surface: Time to eat whatever is served in a bowl or a basin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuck into' looks like eating, but it places T inside SOUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A holy-water basin at a church entrance is called by this name.

clue.text: In city once caught by demand for evidence of status

indicators.note: one letter sits in the middle of the old city name

parts.note: Peking is the former Western name of Beijing
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an order is a demand or command

explanation.surface: Someone in an old city was caught out by a call for proof of their standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A social hierarchy, as among hens pecking, shows who ranks above whom.

clue.text: One coming out for some bread

definitions.meaning: a flower or plant that is opening up its petals
a crusty loaf with diagonal slashes across its top

explanation.definitionFit: A plant in flower and a British loaf both carry this name, a pair of separate senses.

clue.text: Pass down the generations new human life? Endlessly trying

indicators.note: a new version is a remade one, so the letters are put in fresh order
without its end, the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A new human life is being made, after endless trying, to continue the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts TRYING to TRYIN; 'new' rearranges it with HUMAN LIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait inherited from parent to child is said to be common to a whole line of relatives.

clue.text: Carrying a seal? Short contribution to power

indicators.note: something short is cut down, here by its last letter

parts.note: an input is a contribution
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A question about a seal, followed by a brief remark about electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops T from INPUT, then P is added. A baby seal is a pup, so a pregnant seal is carrying one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pregnant animal carries its young, and a baby seal is a pup, so this describes an expectant seal.

clue.text: Monocle, say, impressing you, a girl

indicators.note: pressing in, so one word is pushed into another

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does
ye is an old word for you
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A monocle makes an impression on a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A single lens worn in one eye is one example of a corrective lens of this type.

clue.text: A lot of laughter is appropriate

definitions.meaning: ... of laughter are bouts of it
is suitable or the right shape and size

explanation.surface: A great deal of laughing turns out to be quite right.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means sudden bursts, and the verb means suits or matches correctly.

clue.text: Electrical equipment officer almost gets to run

indicators.note: almost all of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An officer nearly manages to run something electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that converts motion into electric current is a piece of electrical kit.

clue.text: Disappointment with extremes of temperature? Be ambivalent

parts.note: a blow is a setback or disappointment
the two ends of the temperature scale

explanation.surface: Being let down by weather that swings between very warm and very chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternating enthusiasm and coolness is an idiom for being undecided or inconsistent.

clue.text: City all spread out?

parts.note: read as nothing (O) and crowded, a city with zero density would be all spread out

explanation.surface: A question about a sprawling city.
explanation.walkthrough: The Danish city on Funen, birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen, splits into O and DENSE: 'zero dense', i.e. spread out.
explanation.definitionFit: This Danish city on the island of Funen is the birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen.

clue.text: Next to assistant, is keen to join in

indicators.note: joining in means entering the middle of the other word

parts.note: an aide is an assistant
someone who longs for something is keen on it

explanation.surface: Beside a helper, someone is eager to take part.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beside something is a synonym for being next to it.

clue.text: Devastated by strain that breaks cricket practice up

indicators.note: breaking into something splits it apart with the other piece in the gap
in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: nets are the netted practice areas where cricketers train
to rick is to sprain or strain a joint

explanation.surface: A cricketer is ruined by an injury that stops training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NETS into STEN, and RICK 'breaks' it: ST-RICK-EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being struck down by grief or illness leaves one devastated, a close synonym.

clue.text: Man originally interrupts me to make polite address

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the other word

parts.note: Adam was the original man in Genesis

explanation.surface: A man butts in on me to speak courteously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man originally' looks like a first-letter signal giving M, but it is ADAM, the first man.
explanation.definitionFit: A courteous French form of addressing a woman, used in English too.

clue.text: Son gets sort of van to run fast

parts.note: a camper is a camper van

explanation.surface: A son gets a camper van to dash about in.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash quickly with small steps is a synonym for running fast.

clue.text: Mess up putting diamonds among paste

indicators.note: putting something among others places it inside them

parts.note: miso is a Japanese fermented soybean paste
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone botches jewellery making by putting real gems among fake paste stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Paste suggests fake jewels beside diamonds, but it is the Japanese soybean paste.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something wrongly is to botch it or mess it up.

clue.text: Bird left where all birds were gathered

parts.note: Noah's ark held all the birds and animals during the Flood

explanation.surface: A bird flew off from the place where every bird had been gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: The skylark is a songbird, so this is a type of bird.
